source_of_truth.maintenance_model: Repo-maintained workload map with live links for volatile model and provider inventory.
freshness_boundaries: Treat the workload grouping in this file as stable repo guidance, but resolve live model inventory from the linked runtime surfaces before automation.
Assistant model IDs can change by region or account. Verify them with GET /v2/ai/models, telnyx ai models, or the current AI Assistants docs before scripting against a specific ID.
Inference model availability changes faster than repo releases. Verify it with the live inference model catalog or API before assuming a model is still available.

workloads.name: Hosted voice assistants on Telnyx
workloads.summary: Use Telnyx-managed assistants when you want telephony, speech, and assistant runtime on one platform.
choose_when: You want the assistant runtime, telephony, STT, and TTS managed inside Telnyx.
You want fast first-run voice evaluation from the portal or Assistants API.
You want built-in assistant features such as workflow routing, memory, handoff, or traffic testing.
workloads.freshness_note: Do not pin a hosted assistant model from this repo alone. Resolve the current assistant catalog at runtime, then keep only the chosen model ID in your deployment config.

workloads.name: Telnyx-hosted inference and embeddings
workloads.summary: Use the OpenAI-compatible inference surface when you want stateless model calls, embeddings, or non-voice agent workloads.
choose_when: You need chat completions or embeddings without the full voice-assistant runtime.
You want model choice at request time through an OpenAI-compatible API.
You want to evaluate new hosted inference models as the catalog changes.
workloads.freshness_note: Inference inventory is intentionally live-linked. Release notes may announce a model before this repo updates, so verify the runtime catalog before assuming availability.

workloads.name: External LLM or agent stack on Telnyx voice
workloads.summary: Keep Telnyx as the telecom and speech layer while an external AI engine owns reasoning or application logic.
choose_when: You already run your own model gateway, OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or agent runtime.
You need a provider or model that is not in the hosted assistant catalog.
You want to preserve more application-layer control while keeping Telnyx telephony.
workloads.freshness_note: This path is capability-stable but provider-specific. Validate the external endpoint contract and any custom model IDs directly against your own runtime.

workloads.name: Conversation Relay for text-streaming voice AI
workloads.summary: Use Conversation Relay when you want Telnyx telephony plus STT/TTS, but your app prefers text over raw-audio media streams.
choose_when: Your AI stack already consumes text turns and should not ingest raw RTP or media frames.
You want WebSocket text streaming between live calls and your AI logic.
You want a lighter bridge from Telnyx voice into CRM, chatbot, or custom NLU workflows.

execution_entrypoints: Voice API start conversation relay command

workloads.freshness_note: Conversation Relay is a fast-moving orchestration surface. Treat the release note and current Voice API docs as the canonical contract before rollout.

workloads.name: Structured assistant orchestration
workloads.summary: Use workflows, handoff, async tools, and traffic testing when one assistant needs staged reasoning, specialist routing, or controlled rollout.
choose_when: A single prompt is too broad and the conversation needs distinct stages.
You need per-step model or voice overrides, deterministic edges, or assistant-to-assistant routing.
You want to test prompts, voices, or models gradually before promotion.
workloads.freshness_note: These orchestration primitives evolve quickly. Use the live docs for field-level payload details even when this repo gives the right workload starting point.

operational_notes: The repo is the source of truth for workload grouping and public discovery URLs, not for a guaranteed live model inventory.
Use release notes for recency, but use the linked docs or runtime catalog for the contract you automate against.
When a workload needs account-specific or region-specific model availability, preserve the resolved model ID in your own config after runtime discovery.

risk_classes.read_only: Discovery or inspection only. No account mutation or external side effect is expected.
risk_classes.guarded_write: Billed execution or account-scoped mutation may occur. Confirm intent before mutating state.
risk_classes.live_write: Can send traffic, move money, provision resources, or change regulated production state. Explicit approval is expected before execution.

approval_expectations.none: No extra approval is expected beyond normal caller authorization.
approval_expectations.confirm_before_mutation: Obtain human or policy confirmation before any state-changing or billed execution.
approval_expectations.confirm_before_external_effect: Obtain explicit human or policy approval before sending traffic, spending funds, or provisioning live resources.

approval_paths.none_read_only: Read-only discovery or inspection. Persist returned request identifiers for traceability when needed.
approval_paths.confirm_intent_then_mutate: Capture user or policy confirmation and preserve request-scoped identifiers before any billed or state-changing execution.
approval_paths.explicit_approval_then_execute: Require explicit operator approval, then retain the returned identifiers needed to review external effects, provisioning, or spend.

memory_scopes.stateless: The surface does not retain conversation state unless the caller supplies it.
memory_scopes.host_controlled: Persistence, if any, is owned by Telnyx or the host system rather than the model runtime.
memory_scopes.customer_configured: The customer configures the memory or conversation-retention behavior for this capability.
memory_scopes.app_scoped: State is bounded to the MCP app or workflow contract rather than the full Telnyx account surface.

model_behaviors.host_controlled: No model behavior is exposed at this discovery layer, or execution is not model-driven.
model_behaviors.request_selected: The caller chooses the model at request time.
model_behaviors.customer_configured: The customer selects and configures the model during resource setup.
model_behaviors.app_defined: Model behavior is constrained by the governed app or workflow surface.

audit_identifier_legend.request_id: Request-scoped correlation identifier returned by the surface or retained in logs.
audit_identifier_legend.resource_id: Identifier of the created or mutated Telnyx resource being acted on or reviewed later.
audit_identifier_legend.idempotency_key: Caller-supplied key used to deduplicate retries or confirm operator intent.
audit_identifier_legend.model_id: Model identifier selected or returned for AI inference and evaluation flows.
audit_identifier_legend.conversation_id: Conversation or session identifier for assistant or workflow review.
audit_identifier_legend.webhook_delivery_id: Webhook or event-delivery identifier used to reconcile downstream effects.
